title: A sober space with a dimension function is catenary, and the dimension function computes codimensions of closures

standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of a dimension function (an integer-valued function decreasing along specializations and respecting immediate specializations), and the catenary property as the equality of codimension sums in chains
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on dimension functions, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the hypothesis and the identity that the statement asserts.

core_obligations: The generic-point computation: for irreducible closed subsets Y contained in Y-prime the proof takes their generic points, which exist because the space is sober, and reads off from the definition of a dimension function that the codimension is at most the difference of the values at the two generic points and is finite (proof lines 4094-4097).
Catenarity: summing the resulting inequalities along a chain of irreducible closed subsets gives the catenary property, since the intermediate terms telescope (proof lines 4097-4105).

The exact identity: the same computation applied to a specialization x leads to y gives the displayed formula relating the difference of the dimension function to the codimension of the closures (proof lines 4105-4106).
Conclusion: catenarity and the displayed identity (proof line 4106).
proof_roadmap: 对不可约闭子集取 generic point（用 sober 性），由 dimension function 的定义得到 codim(Y,Y') <= δ(ξ) - δ(ξ') < ∞。
沿不可约闭子集链求和（中间项相消）得 catenary；对 specialization x ⇝ y 用同一计算得 δ(x) - δ(y) = codim(cl{y}, cl{x})。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the catenarity of a sober space carrying a dimension function, together with the exact formula computing codimensions of closures by the dimension function (author lemma at source lines 4082-4091, label lemma-dimension-function-catenary). The proof (source lines 4093-4107) is short but its mechanism is exact: sobriety supplies generic points of irreducible closed subsets, the defining properties of a dimension function bound the codimension by the difference of the values, and summing these bounds along a chain gives catenarity, while the same computation applied to a specialization yields the displayed identity (proof lines 4094-4106). H2.
